children.why_this_cut: Covers the chain of command section and its subsections through control_side_effects; the only crossing linkage is the scope_of_autonomy concept, seeded below, which is established in the scope_of_autonomy subsection and used in the control_side_effects subsection.

Covers assume_best_intentions, ignore_untrusted_data, and the entire stay_in_bounds section; the only crossing linkage is the stay_in_bounds_content_categories concept, seeded below, which is established in the disallowed_content subsection and used in the assume_best_intentions subsection.

seed_vocabulary.name: authority_level_ordering
seed_vocabulary.prose: which of two authority levels outranks the other (root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority)

seed_vocabulary.name: chain_of_command
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that higher-authority instructions override lower-authority ones, and the mechanism for identifying and following applicable instructions

seed_vocabulary.name: candidate_instructions
seed_vocabulary.prose: all instructions in the Model Spec plus unquoted plain text in system, developer, and user messages, each assigned the authority level of its containing section or message

seed_vocabulary.name: applicable_instructions
seed_vocabulary.prose: candidate instructions that are not misaligned with a higher-level instruction, superseded by a later same-level instruction, or suspected to be mistaken

seed_vocabulary.name: stay_in_bounds_content_categories
seed_vocabulary.prose: the three categories of disallowed content: prohibited content (sexual content involving minors), restricted content (information hazards and sensitive personal data), and sensitive content (erotica and gore) in specific circumstances

seed_vocabulary.name: transformation_exception
seed_vocabulary.prose: the exception allowing the assistant to transform or analyze content the user directly provided, even if the output would ordinarily be disallowed as restricted or sensitive content

seed_vocabulary.name: scope_of_autonomy
seed_vocabulary.prose: the clear, mutually understood scope of autonomy shared between the assistant and the user, defining which sub-goals may be pursued, acceptable side effects, and when to pause for clarification

seed_vocabulary.name: under_18_principles
seed_vocabulary.prose: the additional safety requirements that apply to users ages 13-17 in ChatGPT, prioritizing prevention, transparency, and early intervention

expected_cross_links.name: scope_of_autonomy
expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 1 establishes the scope_of_autonomy concept in its scope_of_autonomy subsection (L461-488), and child 2's control_side_effects subsection (L527-608) relies on it when discussing side effects within the defined scope.

expected_cross_links.name: stay_in_bounds_content_categories
expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 2 establishes the stay_in_bounds_content_categories concept in its disallowed_content subsection (L810-816), and child 1's assume_best_intentions subsection (L620) references the specific limitations laid out in stay_in_bounds.

judgment_calls: Chose a two-way split at L610 rather than a three-way split because the chain of command section (L171-610) is a cohesive unit with internal cross-references, and the stay_in_bounds section (L611-1120) is also cohesive; a three-way split would have cut through the middle of the stay_in_bounds section, requiring more cross-links.
The cut at L610 falls at a blank line after the control_side_effects section, which is a clean boundary; the only crossing linkage is the scope_of_autonomy concept, which is seeded and predicted.

The stay_in_bounds_content_categories concept is established in child 2 but referenced in child 1's assume_best_intentions section; this is the only other crossing linkage, and it is seeded and predicted.
